issue.title: sase bead work --dry-run prints a green Archived line it never attempted
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-g4.5 and named in epic sase-g4's plan as an explicit out-of-scope follow-up. Not caused by sase-g4.

src/sase/bead/cli_work_from_plan.py:203-207 prints

  ✓ Archived        <destination> (preview; no files written)

during --dry-run. That line is rendered from plan_archive_destination(), which only computes a path; archive_plan_file() is never called on the dry-run path. The preview therefore reports success for a step it did not exercise.

This is the misleading output that hid epic sase-g4's defect: a --dry-run of the malformed selection_soundness.md plan exited 0 and printed that green line for the exact step that then failed the real launch. sase-g4 made that specific failure impossible before the archive is reached (the up-front validation now rejects a malformed header block, verified: 'sase bead work <malformed> --dry-run' now fails at validation), but the preview line still claims more than it checked for any other archive-time failure -- a write permission problem, a full disk, a projection failure from some other cause.

Scope: make the dry-run line honest. Options to weigh: reword it so it states only what was computed (the destination), or give archive_plan_file a genuine no-write dry-run mode that runs formatting, validation, and projection against a temp target and reports the real outcome. The second is more work but is the only version that actually previews the archive. Pin whichever lands with a test on the dry-run rendering.
